title: coppice lane urgent care ramp forecast
instruction:
You are the medical and health services manager supporting Dunmarrow Housing Trust’s Coppice Lane Urgent Care opening on 15 September. Delphine Montague needs the operating outlook settled before provider commitments enter their six-week lead-time window, because the site opens directly into respiratory season and early demand could give a misleading picture of the level it can afford to carry into March. The planning evidence is in `Coppice_Lane_planning_pack.xlsx`, which combines the opening operating position, demand and ramp assumptions, scheduled events, provider capacity, pay information, and the service and financial controls applicable in England as at 31 July 2026. Please produce a twenty-week site ramp forecast showing the low, central, and high demand scenarios, the resulting provider staffing and weekly budget position, and the specific weekly observed-volume thresholds that distinguish adding the second provider shift, holding the current pattern, and cutting evening hours. Show the decision week and the week in which each decision could take effect, and make clear how the first six weeks, the partial opening week, respiratory season, planned events, closures, and any unavailable evidence affect the figures. The forecast should separate sourced facts from assumptions and exclusions, retain enough calculation detail for Antoni Asante to trace the weekly totals, and include a concise plain-language summary suitable for publication to residents and other non-specialist readers. Present the options and their consequences neutrally rather than recommending a staffing action, and do not describe forecast values as actual activity. Return one workbook named exactly `Coppice_Lane_site_ramp_forecast.xlsx`, written at the top level of the working directory you start in. Keep the workbook practical for weekly use, with visible units, scenario labels, trigger definitions, budget totals, and source references; do not carry forward any unsupported value merely because it appears in an old summary calculation.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/Coppice_Lane_planning_pack.xlsx` — Supplies the opening operating state, dated planning events, demand and seasonal assumptions, capacity and cost inputs, and the service and financial controls needed for the twenty-week forecast.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `Coppice_Lane_site_ramp_forecast.xlsx` — A twenty-week site ramp forecast, staffing-trigger schedule, weekly budget outlook, assumptions and exclusions record, and public-facing summary. (Write the file at the top level of the starting working directory.; Use the exact filename Coppice_Lane_site_ramp_forecast.xlsx.; Cover twenty consecutive operating weeks beginning with the partial opening week.; Include low, central, and high demand scenarios.; Show weekly add, hold, and cut trigger thresholds with decision and effective weeks.; Separate sourced facts from assumptions and exclusions.; Present facts and options neutrally for a broad non-specialist audience.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

sheets.name: Public Summary
rows: Coppice Lane Urgent Care | twenty-week site ramp forecast
Forecast scenarios for residents and stakeholders | England controls as at 31 July 2026
This workbook shows modeled demand, capacity and budget; values are forecasts, not actual patient activity.

Modeled weekly demand ranges from 0 to 588 visits across the scenarios. Respiratory-season factors temporarily lift demand above the underlying ramp; the later normalized run-rate removes that factor.

Staffing decisions are assessed weekly using observed-volume thresholds. An add, hold, or cut outcome is conditional; the workbook does not recommend an action. Decisions need six weeks before they could affect staffing, so late-horizon effects are shown as outside the forecast.

Limitations: one outreach event has no measurable effect and is excluded numerically; opening-week evening share uses the bounded scenario profile. Keys are matched after trimming and case normalization, and the prior summary error is rebuilt from valid detail.

spec.professional_context: Dunmarrow Housing Trust is preparing to open Coppice Lane Urgent Care in England during respiratory season. Delphine Montague needs a public-facing ramp forecast and pre-agreed staffing triggers before provider commitments enter their lead-time window.
difficulty_sources: Replaying a partial opening week, dated events, operating exceptions, ramp progression, and delayed staffing changes as a stateful forecast
Separating temporary respiratory-season demand from the site's underlying mature run-rate
Balancing service-capacity and affordability controls when deriving weekly add, hold, and cut thresholds
Reconciling case and whitespace variants in join keys without merging genuinely different records
Handling a noisy floating-point rate and rejecting a residual erroneous summary formula
Making bounded, visible judgments for missing event-effect and evening-share evidence
Explaining technical trigger and budget results neutrally for a broad non-specialist audience

semantic_contents: An opening-state record with the opening date, initial provider pattern, operating sessions, starting awareness or ramp state, and the site's mature weekly demand basis.
Scenario assumptions for low, central, and high demand, including weekly state progression, retention or organic growth effects, and a mature-state ceiling.
A calendar-indexed respiratory-season series covering the full forecast horizon and a later non-peak factor for the normalized run-rate view.
A dated event and operating-exception log containing supported outreach effects, temporary closures, and reduced sessions.
Provider schedules, paid hours, throughput assumptions, first-provider capacity, incremental second-provider productivity, and shift-level pay rates.
Revenue or funding assumptions, recurring operating costs, opening-only costs, and event-specific costs.

A genuine management-control extract applicable in England as at the stated date, defining service-capacity, incremental-payroll, evening-viability, and repeated-evidence controls. It should read as an existing operating control, not as solver instructions.
A prior analyst summary area alongside the valid detail, including the seeded residual formula error.
Short text notes supplying the context and provenance of assumptions so the workbook is a mixed-format evidence bundle.

missing_evidence.gap: One planned outreach event has a date and description but no measurable attendance or demand-effect field.
missing_evidence.expected_treatment: Do not invent a point uplift. Exclude the numeric effect or use a clearly bounded scenario assumption, identify the affected week, and disclose the treatment.

missing_evidence.gap: The opening-week evening share is absent while an analogous-site range is supplied elsewhere in the pack.
missing_evidence.expected_treatment: A practitioner may use a bounded assumption from the analogous-site range, but must label it as an assumption and apply it consistently.

seeded_layout_defects.implementation: Use logically identical identifiers such as `EVENING-A`, `evening-a `, and `Evening-A` across the event, capacity, and rate records. No other malformed keys, duplicate records, shifted headers, hidden tables, or layout traps are present.
seeded_layout_defects.gold_rule: Match after trimming surrounding whitespace and normalizing case only; do not collapse identifiers that remain substantively different after that normalization.

seeded_layout_defects.implementation: Store the intended provider unit rate as 187.6300000004 in one detailed source record while the corresponding control or category boundary is represented as 187.63.
seeded_layout_defects.gold_rule: Treat these as the same economic rate using currency-aware rounding or a suitable tolerance. Weekly currency results are evaluated to the nearest penny, not by exact binary equality.

seeded_layout_defects.implementation: Place a prior analyst summary formula equivalent to `=SUM(valid_detail_range)+#REF!` in a summary cell that purports to show a demand subtotal. Valid detailed records needed to rebuild the subtotal remain intact.
seeded_layout_defects.gold_rule: Ignore the erroneous summary formula and reconstruct the affected metric from valid detail. No output formula may depend on the error cell.

state_replay.opening_state: Start each scenario from the supplied opening ramp and staffing states. The first interval is a partial operating week beginning on the opening date.
state_replay.weekly_transition: Advance the demand-ramp state from the preceding week's state using the matching scenario progression and retention parameters, then enforce the supplied mature-state ceiling.
state_replay.dated_events: Apply supported event effects only in their dated periods. Apply closures and reduced sessions to operating availability for their dates, then return to the normal schedule.
state_replay.demand_rule: For each scenario and week, derive session or daypart demand from mature demand, current ramp state, calendar seasonal factor, available sessions, and supported event effects. Weekly totals equal their components.
state_replay.staffing_rule: Begin with the supplied staffing state. A qualifying decision in week t may alter the staffing state only in week t plus the supplied six-week lead interval. Continue the prior state during the intervening weeks.
state_replay.late_horizon_rule: Decisions whose effective dates fall after the twentieth forecast week remain visible as out-of-horizon effects and do not alter an earlier week.

trigger_derivation.observed_volume_mapping: For each eligible decision week, use the supplied scenario state and seasonal relationships to map an observed weekly volume to expected demand in the effective week after the lead interval.
trigger_derivation.add_boundary: Derive the minimum whole observed-volume threshold whose mapped effective-week demand breaches the first-provider service-capacity control and whose incremental second-shift economics meet the supplied payroll or contribution control. If the two controls imply different boundaries, the add threshold must satisfy both.
trigger_derivation.cut_boundary: Derive the maximum whole observed-volume threshold whose mapped effective-week evening activity falls below the supplied viability control while respecting any access floor.
trigger_derivation.repeated_evidence: Replay the supplied consecutive-low-observation control before a cut classification becomes available.
trigger_derivation.hold_band: Define hold as the complete interval between the cut and add decisions, with explicit and consistent endpoint inequalities.
trigger_derivation.rounding: Round thresholds to whole visits in a direction that preserves control compliance; retain unrounded calculations for traceability.
trigger_derivation.seasonal_tradeoff: The early peak-season factor must not be treated as evidence that the site has already reached mature steady state. Include a later normalized run-rate by removing the temporary peak factor from the later ramp state.

capacity_and_budget_rules.first_provider_capacity: Scheduled provider hours multiplied by the matching throughput rate and operating availability.
capacity_and_budget_rules.second_provider_capacity: Incremental hours and the supplied overlap or productivity factor, calculated separately from first-provider capacity.
capacity_and_budget_rules.provider_cost: Paid hours multiplied by normalized matching rates, rounded to currency only for displayed results.
capacity_and_budget_rules.revenue_or_funding: Modeled activity multiplied by the matching unit amount, with any supplied caps or bounds applied.
capacity_and_budget_rules.weekly_balance: Revenue or funding less baseline provider payroll, effective incremental-shift payroll, and applicable operating costs.
capacity_and_budget_rules.cumulative_balance: Opening cumulative position plus the ordered sum of weekly balances.
capacity_and_budget_rules.totals: Twenty-week totals equal sums of unrounded weekly calculations, displayed to the nearest penny.

gold_generation.method: Use an offline reference script to parse valid source detail, normalize join keys, replay the twenty weekly states, derive scenario demand and capacity, calculate weekly trigger boundaries, apply delayed staffing transitions, and calculate budget lines and totals.
relational_outputs: Twenty consecutive weekly states and scenario forecasts.
Weekly first-provider and incremental second-provider capacities.
Whole-volume add, hold, and cut boundaries.
Weekly staffing state and budget under the replay.
gold_generation.verification: Independently recompute representative opening, seasonal-peak, event, closure, transition, and late-horizon weeks; scan the generated solution for spreadsheet errors; render it to verify legibility; then have a domain reviewer assess assumptions, trigger tradeoffs, neutrality, and public comprehensibility.

expected_disclosures: The treatment of the outreach event lacking a measurable effect.
The bounded assumption used for the absent opening-week evening share, if used.
Normalization of case and trailing whitespace in keys.
Currency-aware handling of the noisy rate.
Exclusion and rebuilding of the erroneous prior summary.
The distinction between respiratory-season demand and underlying mature demand.
The scenario basis used for the published trigger table.
The fact that late-horizon decisions take effect outside the forecast.

deliverables.description: A twenty-week site ramp forecast, staffing-trigger schedule, weekly budget outlook, assumptions and exclusions record, and public-facing summary.
constraints: Write the file at the top level of the starting working directory.
Cover twenty consecutive operating weeks beginning with the partial opening week.
Include low, central, and high demand scenarios.
